channel.title: Warp Blog
channel.description: Stories from the Warp team on building the agentic development environment — engineering deep-dives, product launches, terminal performance, AI agents, and how developers use Warp.

item.title: Tactics for rolling out software factories: human and organizational changes
item.description: How to roll out software factories across an engineering org: start with chore automations, meet engineers in their tools, and track factory adoption.
item.dc:creator: Zach Lloyd

item.title: The road to self-improving software
item.description: Let agents decide what to build next: self-improving software factories that proactively fix bugs, refine their own skills, and mine user feedback for roadmap work.
item.dc:creator: Ben Holmes

item.title: Warp Factories now works across Microsoft Teams and Azure DevOps
item.description: Warp Factories now integrates natively with Microsoft Teams and Azure DevOps. Delegate work to your agent software factory from Teams threads, Azure DevOps work items, and pull requests.

item.title: Build the factory. Let it run. Go kayaking.
item.description: During Warp team's Savannah off-site, we focused on making Warp Factories reliable, fast, and cost-effective. Then, we let the agents run while we went kayaking.
item.dc:creator: Ben Holmes

item.title: Terraform for agents: how we define our software factory in code
item.description: We define every agent in our software factory as code: orchestration, secrets, MCP servers, automations, runners, scorers, and benchmarks. Here’s a walkthrough of each part of the factory config.
item.dc:creator: Ben Holmes

item.title: Sign in to Warp with ChatGPT
item.description: Use your ChatGPT subscription for AI requests in Warp Terminal and Warp Agent CLI.

item.title: Adapting for a world of software factories
item.description: Software factories change what engineers do. At Warp, engineers now have two jobs: building the product, and building the factory that builds the product.
item.dc:creator: Zach Lloyd

item.title: Using LLM-as-a-judge scoring to measure your software factory
item.description: If you want to get the most out of coding agents in your organization, you need to stop guessing how well your agents are performing and start measuring.
item.dc:creator: Zach Lloyd

item.title: Adopting the software factory model: crawl, walk, run
item.description: A crawl, walk, run path for adopting the software factory model: start with point automations, stand up an end-to-end cloud development loop, then scale to a closed-loop factory stack.
item.dc:creator: Zach Lloyd

item.title: The Factory Stack
item.description: Software factories should be built on an infrastructure stack that is open, composable and defined in code.
item.dc:creator: Zach Lloyd

item.title: Introducing Factory Benchmarks
item.description: Today we are launching Benchmarks in Warp Factories early access: agent benchmarks on your own code that drive direct improvements in software factory performance. Rather than guessing at what model and skill configurations are best, you can now easily test, measure, and put your findings into practice.
item.dc:creator: Zach Lloyd

item.title: WarpBench: How we reduced our cost-per-PR 75%
item.description: With Warp Factories Benchmarking, it’s now possible to build custom coding agent benchmarks on your team’s real data and workflows with a few clicks.
item.dc:creator: Zach Lloyd
